scope: Estonia medical discovery — University of Tartu Faculty of Medicine

verifiedFacts.claim: University of Tartu's 2026–27 English Medicine curriculum is an integrated bachelor's and master's programme in Tartu lasting six years and 360 ECTS, with 24 student places and EUR 13,200 annual tuition.
The same current curriculum page gives the 2026 Medicine admissions timeline: applications open 2 January, close 15 April, results on 1 June and the academic year starts 31 August.

UT describes the six-year Faculty of Medicine programme as fully in English and says its clinical learning uses actual patients at Tartu University Hospital, Estonia's largest medical-care provider; students learn Estonian for local hospital work.
University of Tartu states it received seven-year institutional accreditation in 2022 from the Estonian Quality Agency and that the next institutional accreditation is scheduled for 2029.
UT's 2026 tuition policy specifies English-programme payment rules and a half-first-semester prepayment requirement for non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants without a qualifying long-term residence permit.

holdReasons: The curriculum page identifies application components, but a complete current programme-specific eligibility, entrance-assessment and document-recognition evidence packet was not completed.
Institutional accreditation is strong but distinct from a complete current programme-specific recognition/graduate-practice badge packet.
